lee: quick note - onboarding Seraph-13B (Gemma-ish) int4. Two reproducible problems: combining diacritics split into separate tokens (e.g. "é" -> ['e','́']) and rotary frequency looks scaled differently per-head after quant.
tara: which converter + tokenizer?
lee: `tools/convert.py --quant=int4-fast --fold-rotary-headwise` and tokenizer shipped with model had `normalize: false`. sample token sequence for "Café": [101,2048,13723,3].
mike: sounds like missing NFC/NFKC normalization. For the rotary, if folding applied headwise scales into table a bug could alter phase slope. can you run with pre-normalize and without fold?
lee: ran NFC pre-normalize -> tokens collapse to single "é" token. rerun convert without `--fold-rotary-headwise` -> head phase slopes match fp32. quick 10-doc rouge/qa check: folded-int4 vs fp32 -1.1, unfolder-int4 vs fp32 -0.08.
yara: ok actionable: 1) enable NFC pre-tokenize in ingestion pipeline (unit test), 2) make headwise rotary folding opt-in and add converter regression test, 3) larger eval (200 samples) to confirm.
ci-bot: ci/onboard-seraph triggered: tokenization/regression flaky.
lee: opening PRs for tokenizer normalizer + converter opt-in. tagging mike for review. thanks. :white_check_mark:
